extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant reviewers and immunology/epigenetics researchers proposing or evaluating mechanistic Treg/EZH2 studies
extracted.subtask_description: Research strategy text from an NIH-style R01 describing specific aims, experimental approaches, anticipated results, alternatives, and translational plans to define EZH2 function in FOXP3+ Treg cells and to develop engineered Treg therapies for IBD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test requirement of EZH2–FOXP3 physical interaction by luciferase assay
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine relevance of FOXP3 to EZH2 function through quantitative luciferase assay; perform identical assays utilizing EZH2 and FOXP3 domain mutants to test the requirement of EZH2 and FOXP3 physical interaction for repressor function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use titrated quantities of FOXP3 in reporter cell lines, include WT and domain-mutant EZH2/FOXP3 constructs (see Figure 7). Expect WT EZH2 (with FOXP3) to repress reporters; mutants predicted to disrupt recruitment should fail to repress. Provide explicit constructs and dose–response conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ChIP assay for H3K27me3, EZH2 and FOXP3 at target promoters
rubrics_metrics.description: Assay presence and function of EZH2 at particular promoter loci using Chromatin Immunoprecipitation (ChIP) for the H3K27me3 histone “mark” and for EZH2 and FOXP3 at RORA and IRF4 promoters in FOXP3ΔEZH2 Treg cells transduced with WT or EZH2 mutant constructs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require FOXP3ΔEZH2 mouse colony and adenoviral WT or EZH2 mutant constructs; use CAR-transgenic background for efficient adenoviral transduction of resting lymphocytes. Cite laboratory’s published ChIP and adenoviral transduction experience. Expect deposition of H3K27me3 with WT but not with mutants that disrupt FOXP3 recruitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vitro Treg suppression assay with defined stimulation and titration
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-culture naïve FOXP3- CD4+ T responder cells with titrated amounts of Treg cells under TCR stimulation (anti-CD3, anti-CD28) to assess suppressor function of FOXP3ΔEZH2 Treg cells transduced with WT or mutant EZH2 constructs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use titrations of Treg:Tresp ratios, standardized stimulation conditions, and transduction with WT and mutant constructs to test dependence of suppressor function on EZH2–FOXP3 complex formation. Report controls and replicate numbers; statistical testing (e.g., p<0.05) for suppression differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo CD45Rbhi → RAGnull colitis model to test Treg prevention and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the CD45Rbhi transfer model into RAGnull mice (with or without co-transfer of FOXP3+ Treg cells) to test in vivo function of FOXP3ΔEZH2 Treg cells and rescue by WT EZH2 or failure by EZH2 mutants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify cell numbers (example: 350,000 naïve CD4+ alone or with 100,000 FOXP3+ Treg cells), tamoxifen-inducible CRE for conditional EZH2 deletion, and adenoviral transduction of constructs. Assess colitis severity by disease activity index (DAI), blinded histology, cytokine profiles from mesenteric lymph nodes and colonic supernatants. Include sample sizes and blinded outcome assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit Anticipated Results, potential pitfalls, and alternative approaches section
rubrics_metrics.description: State clear expectations for outcomes (e.g., EZH2 complexes with FOXP3, WT represses targets only with FOXP3, functional relevance in suppression and colitis prevention) and enumerate alternative hypotheses and approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss concrete alternatives (e.g., indirect interaction via EED/Suz12 — test by siRNA knockdown and repeat Co-IP; EZH2 localization via ncRNA — test by cross-linking immunoprecipitation combined with RNAseq) and contingency experimental plans. This strengthens feasibility and reviewer confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a complementary experimental pipeline (bioinformatics → MS → modeling → mutational screens → functional assays)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine bioinformatic prediction of post‑translational modification sites, mass spectrometry confirmation, molecular modeling, mutational screens, and functional biochemical/cellular assays to identify mechanisms regulating EZH2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify pipeline rationale: breadth of discovery (MS) balanced by focused confirmations (WB) and mechanistic tests (mutants, modeling). Present preliminary data to show pipeline feasibility and expected interpretative flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthogonal confirmation of phosphorylation and kinase involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify EZH2 phosphorylation sites by MS and confirm by western blot using phospho‑site antibodies; test kinase involvement (e.g., JAK2) with pharmacologic inhibitors, siRNA, dominant negatives, and constitutively active constructs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple methods to confirm phosphorylation (MS for discovery, phospho‑antibody for rapid assays). Inhibit JAK2 via AZD1480, siRNA, and dominant-negative constructs; include constitutively active JAK2 V617F as gain‑of‑function control. Use FOXP3ΔIL6Rα Treg cells as relevant negative control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational mutational analysis using phosphomimetic and non‑phosphorylatable mutants
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate mutants designed to mimic phosphorylation (S→D, Y→E) or prevent it (S→A, Y→F) and compare activity to WT in an EZH2KO background (e.g., CRISPR/CAS EZH2KO HAP‑1 cells) using HMT assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen mutants in a controlled EZH2‑null system to attribute HMT differences to the mutation. Provide expectations (e.g., Y641E inactive, Y641F hyperactive) and use adenoviral constructs for primary cell confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole‑cell functional assays linking biochemical modifications to gene regulation and cell function
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate biochemical effects (SET domain phosphorylation) to whole‑cell outcomes: genomically integrated luciferase reporters driven by RORA/IRF4 promoters and in vitro suppression assays under IL6 stimulation with WT and mutant EZH2 constructs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use integrated reporters (Jurkat FLP system) rather than episomal plasmids for stable readouts. Expect that phosphomimetic mutants de‑repress reporters and impair suppression, whereas non‑phosphorylatable mutants retain function even with IL6. Correlate reporter data with suppression assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical and outcome‑assessment rigor including blinding and predefined metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess disease and experimental outcomes with predefined metrics (DAI, colon length, blinded histology scoring, cytokine ELISA), report sample sizes and statistical significance (example p<0.05).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use blinded histology and objective indices; report n per group, statistical tests, and significance thresholds. Provide representative histology and quantitative plots to support claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate feasibility via preliminary data and prior expertise/publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify experimental plans with relevant preliminary data (e.g., prior observations that IL6 represses EZH2 HMT activity, MS detection of Y641 phosphorylation, molecular modeling, in vitro HMT assay results) and published experience in required techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite prior work from the lab showing use of models, assays, and transduction/editing expertise. Use preliminary results (figures and citations) to argue for feasibility of proposed aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational in vivo therapy testing using engineered Treg cells
rubrics_metrics.description: Design preclinical adoptive transfer/treatment studies to test genetically engineered Treg cells (adenoviral transduction of EZH2 mutants or TALEN editing of IL6R) to treat established colitis rather than only prevention studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify treatment timing (e.g., inject into animals with established colitis 4 weeks post T effector transfer), cell titrations (100–300k), and expected therapeutic readouts. For genetic editing, describe nucleofection, GFP selection by FACS, confirmation by flow cytometry, ex vivo expansion, and safety monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address safety and long‑term behavior of engineered mutants
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge oncogenic or adverse risks (e.g., Y641F associated with lymphoma in whole lymphocyte populations) and plan long‑term behavior and toxicity analyses (e.g., scurfy rescue experiments) to assess safety of Treg‑restricted mutations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assays to monitor transformation, long‑term persistence, and off‑target effects; restrict suspect mutations to Treg subset and propose extended phenotyping and rescue models to evaluate toxicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan alternative strategies and broadened mechanistic exploration if primary hypotheses fail
rubrics_metrics.description: If direct FOXP3–EZH2 interaction or phosphorylation model is not supported, plan to test other mechanisms (e.g., alternative kinases/pathways, EZH1 involvement, alternative substrates or complex partners) using the same MS/mutational pipeline and complex isolation approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep pipeline flexible: use MS screens to detect other modifications, isolate complexes to find binding partners/substrates, and apply the same mutational/functional workflow to alternate candidates. State how each alternative would be tested experimentally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate controls and negative controls throughout
rubrics_metrics.description: Include relevant genetic and pharmacologic controls such as FOXP3ΔIL6Rα Treg cells, IL6R‑deficient donor cells, DZNep pharmacologic inhibition of EZH2, and vehicle or WT construct controls to interpret functional effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use negative and positive controls in each assay (e.g., DZNep to mimic EZH2 inhibition, AZD1480 to block JAK2) and include rescue experiments (restoration with WT EZH2) to demonstrate specificity of observed phenotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage core facilities and collaborative expertise for specialized methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage specialized cores and collaborators (e.g., Genetics and Model Systems Core for TALEN editing, collaborators for MS or animal models) and include letters of collaboration and access to needed platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document collaborative resources and core facility plans (who will perform TALEN editing, MS, etc.), which supports feasibility and reviewer confidence. Provide specifics about responsibilities, protocols, and prior joint publications where possible.
